subtype: Approach: staying alone and waiting for others to come [Pitfall]
passage: I'm Ira. When I started at the new school, I sat alone at lunch every day, holding my tiffin, hoping somebody would say 'Come and sit here.' Nobody did. I looked at the door and my tiffin in turn. Later I found out what the class thought: Bhupen told me they'd assumed I liked being alone, because I never looked up. But I looked up. I just never smiled. By Thursday my throat was tight and I ate only half my lunch. Each day was longer than the last. Waiting felt safe, because nobody could say no, but nothing changed either.

qa.q: What did Ira hold while sitting alone at lunch?
What was Ira feeling by Thursday, and what shows it?
qa.a: Ira felt lonely and sad; the tight throat and half-eaten lunch show it. 😔

qa.q: What alternative approach could Ira try, and why?
qa.a: Ira could smile and say hello to one classmate, or ask the teacher to pair Ira with a friendly buddy. A small step from Ira would give others a sign that company is wanted.

qa.q: How did the class see Ira?
qa.a: The class assumed that Ira liked being alone because Ira never seemed to look up, so they did not go over to Ira.

grounding: Ira sits alone hoping for an invitation, classmates assume it is a choice and stay away, and each day feels lonelier.

subtype: Approach: staying alone and waiting for others to come [Pitfall]
passage:
Class teacher's note, Friday, Class 4B
Farida joined us three weeks ago. Every lunch break she sits on the far bench by the water cooler with her tiffin on her knees, looking at the other children now and then. She does not call to anyone. Today I asked Swati why nobody sits with her. Swati said, "She likes being alone, ma'am. She never talks." I think Farida is waiting to be asked, and the others think she wants to be left alone, so each side is waiting. This week she has begun eating less and looking at the floor more. On Monday I will seat her with Swati's table for a group project and tell her parents what I have seen.

qa.q: Where does Farida sit every lunch break?
qa.a: She sits on the far bench by the water cooler.

qa.q: What might Farida be feeling as she looks at the floor more each week?
qa.a: She is probably lonely and sad, and more discouraged each day that no one comes to her.

qa.q: What else could Farida try, and what could help her do it?
qa.a: She could ask one child if she can sit with them, and a small group project would give her an easy reason to talk.

qa.q: How does Swati see Farida sitting alone?
qa.a: Swati thinks Farida likes being alone because she never talks, so Swati does not try to include her.

grounding: It shows a shy new child waiting alone at lunch, classmates reading her as wanting to be alone, and her loneliness growing.

subtype: Approach: staying alone and waiting for others to come [Pitfall]
passage:
Thursday
Dear diary, day eleven at the new school. I sat on the bench near the swings again at lunch. I brought the good aloo sandwich so if someone came I could share it. Nobody came. Sharmila's group walked past and one of them said, "Leave her, she likes her own company." I don't! I wanted to shout it. But I just looked at my sandwich. Mummy asked how school was and I said fine. It's not fine. It's like being a glass window. Everyone sees me and nobody thinks to come in. Maybe tomorrow I will sit at the end of Sharmila's table. Maybe. My stomach goes funny just writing that.
- Sunaina

qa.q: What did Sunaina bring to lunch to share?
qa.a: Sunaina brought the good aloo sandwich.

qa.q: How did Sunaina feel when Sharmila's group walked past and made that remark?
qa.a: Sunaina felt hurt and misunderstood, wanting to shout that it wasn't true but staying quiet.

qa.q: What would you change first to help Sunaina, and why?
qa.a: Tell Mummy the truth about lunch, because a trusted adult could help with a small step like arranging a partner.

qa.q: How do the girls in Sharmila's group read Sunaina sitting on the bench?
qa.a: They take the silence as liking one's own company, so they think they are being respectful by staying away from Sunaina.

grounding: It shows a shy new child waiting alone for an invitation, being mistaken for wanting to be alone and feeling lonelier.
